content: Melvin-Koushki holds that Ibn Turka, as Akhlāṭī's chief disciple in the east, was animated by the same millenarian ethos as Akhlāṭī and Bedreddīn but expressed it in universalist and intellectual rather than messianic and sociopolitical terms; Akhlāṭī was the prophetic hero and doer, Ibn Turka the apostle and thinker who systematized the master's scattered teachings.
